analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (November 13, 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 gained +2.5% on the week to 7,561.67 despite a hot CPI print, AI infrastructure volatility and a debate over peak earnings growth. NDX rose about 370 bps and SOX about 840 bps, ending a 4-week NDX losing streak. Friday itself closed lower.

Memory (+10.13%), AI Inference Chips (+9.72%), IPPs (+9.44%), Optical Networks (+9.14%) and Datacenters (+8.80%) were the top thematic baskets. Quantum Computing (-9.56%), Goldminers (-7.01%) and Memes (-2.63%) were among the worst.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a 2nd straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by single-stock short sales and partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products. US ETF shorts fell -8.6%, the largest % covering in 7 months. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Financials, Health Care and Staples.

US Financials saw its largest % net selling in 8 months (99th percentile on a 5-year lookback, -2.2 SDs 1-year). Selling was long-and-short at about 4 to 1, and nearly all subsectors except Large Cap Banks were net sold. Financials net exposure is 12.1% of US net MV (98th percentile on a 1-year lookback).

US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5, the lowest on record since 2016 (YTD peak 2.14 in early June). Info Tech was again by far the most net sold sector in dollar terms. Consumer Discretionary was the most net bought US sector (+1.0 SDs), and Staples was net sold on short sales outpacing long buys 5.6 to 1.
US fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile 1-year). Net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile 1-year, 2nd percentile 5-year). Positioning is light.

Share flows: long-only and hedge fund cohorts were both moderate net sellers. There was heavy long-only supply in NVDA, rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. NVDA shed about $500bn of market cap on the week while AMD and AVGO combined added about $500bn+.

Rates and macro: hot CPI on Wednesday and hawkish Fed comments (Waller: a 50bp hike should be conceded at the December meeting) pushed Fed funds futures to price an additional 40bps of hikes by Q3 next year. 2y yields rose 42bps from last Friday's lows and 30y yields rose 25bps, while breakevens stayed relatively stable. The 10y is around 5.13-5.15%, the USD is breaking out, and oil is back in the high-$90s.
Short-term trend signals across the curve flipped negative. The desk expects modest selling over the next week, while the thresholds for larger momentum buying look further out of reach.

Russell 2000 futures funding richened +13bps on Nov 11 (median 1-day change 6bps) after a 5% jump in Retail Favorites. The desk infers the Other and Non-Reportable cohorts may have initiated longs, though they are a small part of open interest. Asset Manager gross longs were positively correlated with SOFR earlier in 2026, so higher-for-longer rate pricing led to liquidation of Russell futures. An extended hiking cycle is flagged as an imminent threat.

Brent fell -20% MTD through Nov 10 and found a floor near $90/bbl. Managed money net length fell -$8bn in the week to Nov 3 and open interest fell a further -$9.3bn through Nov 10. Brent then rebounded +4.7% on stalled negotiations and renewed escalation fears. A +$3bn open interest build on Thursday and Friday desk flows point to fresh length and upside options demand.

Derivatives: US L/S net leverage is near 5-year lows, the Panic Index is 6.5/10, and Nov 5 was the largest put-volume session ever. Index skew is bid, so the 3-month SPX 10% OTM put fully funds a 5.5% OTM call (6.7% OTM this summer), allowing costless collars. Last week was one of the most volatile 'average stock' periods since March 2020, driven by NVDA.

VIX puts traded more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point in 2026. Clients showed more confidence in 'vol lower' than in 'spot higher' after the extreme moves of the prior Thursday.

Momentum: 12m Momentum (GSPRHIMO) had its best outperformance day on record vs 3m (GSPRHMO3) and 6m (GSPRHMO6) momentum on Wednesday. Correlation between 12m and 3m momentum is now negative. AI names in the short leg of 3m and 6m momentum have surged while AI names in the long leg have fallen. Info tech was net sold in 3m and 6m momentum and slightly bought in 12m.

Momentum positioning in the Prime book has collapsed to the 23rd percentile of its 5-year range, and Data Center basket crowding is at the 1st percentile over 6 months. 60-day momentum volatility is about 3.5x the S&P 500. The desk says a resumed rotation could offer tactical shorts in former 12m momentum short names or broadening names (lower-quality software, staples) not supported by fundamentals. Quality could extend its outperformance while 12m Momentum and Beta lag.
Projected momentum rebalances would bring buying of consumer and health care and selling of energy and info tech, specifically a rotation out of semis and into software.

TMT desk: the desk sees relatively little consensus on positioning and sentiment, with debate on where the AI/semi cycle stands and whether this is a bear-market bounce or a new bull market. It described the week's strength as cleaner positioning plus rotations, with software dispersion rising and Internet hard to trade. It calls the 'blank slate' arguably healthy into 2027.

Financials desk: Financials underperformed the SPX by about 200bps with no clear split between defensives and offensives, which suggests positioning drove moves. Consumer Finance had the most negativity on a possibly shifting regulatory backdrop. SCHW was debated: bears cite margin risk from lower October cash and further estimate cuts, bulls call it temporary and point to accelerating organic growth.

Healthcare desk: the sector tracked the market. Hot CPI pushed the 10Y back through 5% and weighed on high-duration areas (SMID biotech, tools/diagnostics). Large biopharma stayed bid (LLY +6%), with valuation 'vertigo' and PFE vs NVDA P/E comparisons circulating. Earnings reactions were harsh: IONS -21% on a sHTG miss and lowered guide, LEGN -24% on the week, TWST -7% and HTFL -18% on beats with raises. NVDA was -13% on the week and -33% since early October.

Industrials desk: industrials +350bps, materials +50bps. SMID AI names led (MOD +43% including +30% Friday on takeout headlines, AAON +40%, CECO +26% on 2027 guide). CTVA fell 22% on a lower implied Q4 outlook (FMC -10%), GFL fell 9% after ending its sale process, and housing names (DFH, LGIH, NX, HOV, NVR) were weak on higher rates.

Energy and utilities desk: 'flight to safety' conversations are elevated. Oil risk premium has dropped over two weeks, gasoline margins are under pressure, and midterm election risk clouds the power complex. Inbounds center on natural gas, with a preference for gas E&Ps (EQT, AR) and midstream (WMB, DTM) on gas volume growth and longer-term power demand.

Week ahead: S&P implied move through Nov 20 is 1.93%. Catalysts are NVDA earnings Tuesday (first report under interim CEO Colette Kress), BABA Thursday, PANW, and consumer prints (TSN, ARMK Mon; HD Tue; TJX, TGT, LOW Wed; WMT, ROST, GAP Thu; BJ Fri). Macro is lighter: US Retail Sales Tuesday and FOMC minutes Wednesday. Also the MSFT Ignite conference and the GTA VI launch (TTWO).
